title: Surrealist founders' occult séances and Breton's 1922 article

tellings.quote: these guys from the beginning of even from before it took the name surrealism were constantly engaged in occult rituals including long seances

plain: The founders of surrealism, the French art movement of the 1920s, were constantly doing occult rituals, including long séances, even before the movement had its name. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says this, naming the poet André Breton, who wrote a 1922 article, along with the painter Max Ernst and the poet Paul Éluard, though he gives no source. If true, one of the great modern art movements grew partly out of attempts to contact spirits.
